page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-48-lssd is an x86_64 virtual server belonging to the general-purpose family, configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 186.0 GB of memory. This hardware allocation provides approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 1611 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage partitioned across four separate drives. The configuration features zero GPU accelerators and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The integration of 1611 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage delivers low latency and high local throughput compared to network-attached block storage. Because local NVMe storage is ephemeral by nature, instances relying on these drives require external data replication or regular backup mechanisms to prevent data loss in the event of host maintenance or instance termination. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance without virtualization thread contention.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, bundling 1611 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity reduces the need to provision premium remote block storage disks to satisfy high IOPS demands. Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-48-lssd is suitable for disk-intensive and transaction-heavy workloads, including relational database replicas, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching layers with local persistence, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-48-lssd is an x86_64 architecture virtual server configured for balanced compute, memory, and high-throughput local storage. It delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs and 186.0 GB of RAM, offering an allocation of roughly 3.88 GB of memory per core. A key differentiator is the inclusion of 1611 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage divided across four drives, providing low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host. The instance contains zero hardware GPU accelerators and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The pairing of 48 dedicated cores with fast local NVMe storage makes this instance economically efficient for high-IOPS applications that would otherwise require expensive provisioned remote block volumes. The c4d-standard-48-lssd is suitable for demanding transactional databases, distributed data processing nodes, search indexing services, caching servers, and local compile or continuous integration workloads.
